question: A ______ is a computer programme which can self-replicate and propagate over the network with or without human intervention and has malicious intent.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Worm.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A **worm**__ is a computer programme that can **self-replicate and propagate over the network with or without human intervention and has malicious intent.**
 
• Its purpose is to secretly **duplicate itself into other computers.**
 
• Unlike a computer virus, which "infects" other programmes in order to spread to new ones, worms are often self-contained programmes that **do not require a "host."**
 
• Worms typically **do not require human intervention** to spread across networks.
 
• **Robert Morris**, a computer science student at Cornell University, unleashed the first worm into the Internet from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology on November 2, 1988.
 
• Viruses and worms are a type of **malicious software.**
 
• Worms frequently take advantage of network configuration mistakes or security flaws in the operating system (OS) or applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• A** kernel** is computer software that runs at the core of the operating system and has complete control over all of the system's components.
 
• A **Trojan Horse **Virus is a sort of malware that disguises itself as a genuine programme and downloads into a computer.
 
• A computer **virus** is designed to spread from host to host and duplicate itself.
